title: Maritime Infrastructure Program (MIP)
eligible_entities: Texas public maritime ports (18 PAAC members incl. Port Freeport)
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Biennial; 90th Legislature cycle in development. Covers docks, cranes, rail, truck queuing, security, facility projects. Port Freeport CEO Phyllis Saathoff serves on PAAC.

title: Seaport Connectivity Program
eligible_entities: Ports and entities for public roadway projects connecting to TX maritime ports
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Biennial; selected through PAAC via Port Mission Plan. $20M/year per biennium; 66 projects cumulative. SH-36/Hwy 288 access improvements are strong candidates.

title: Ship Channel Improvement Revolving Fund (SCIRF)
eligible_entities: Navigation districts and port authorities as non-federal USACE project sponsors
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Rolling via Form 2060-SCIRF. $400M initial capitalization (2023); $200M additional FY2026. Low-interest state loan for USACE-authorized channel projects.

title: Off-System Rail Grade Separation State Fund
eligible_entities: Counties, cities, special districts. Port Freeport partners with Brazoria County.
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Competitive; first round closed Nov 2025; future rounds expected. $250M total program. Projects must be on off-system (non-TxDOT) roads. Port Freeport should partner with local gov.

title: State Infrastructure Bank (SIB)
eligible_entities: Any public or private entity for eligible transportation projects (Title 23/49 USC)
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Rolling <$10M; competitive Program Call for larger. 182 loans totaling $994M+ approved to date. Fixed rate for life of loan, no fees. Best for port access roadway improvements.

title: County Transportation Infrastructure Fund Grant
eligible_entities: Texas counties — Brazoria County as applicant
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Annual. Oil/gas production tax revenue. Indirect benefit to Port Freeport via Brazoria County road improvements.

title: TERP — Port Authority Studies and Pilot Projects (PASPP)
eligible_entities: Port authorities administering a public seaport in a nonattainment area. Port Freeport explicitly eligible.
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Projected opening November 2026; TCEQ contacts eligible port authorities directly. ONLY TERP program designed exclusively for port authorities. Funds air quality studies or pilot projects to reduce NOx/PM.

title: TERP — Seaport and Rail Yard Areas Emissions Reduction (SPRY)
eligible_entities: Entities operating equipment at designated seaports. Port of Freeport explicitly listed.
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Projected opening August 2026 (first-come, first-served). Up to 80% of eligible costs. Covers drayage trucks, terminal tractors, cargo handling equipment, RTG cranes, forklifts. Equipment must operate 200+ days/yr at eligible seaport.

title: TERP — Emissions Reduction Incentive Grants (ERIG)
eligible_entities: Entities in eligible counties including Brazoria County
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Projected opening April 2026. Competitive, scored on cost-per-ton NOx reduced. Covers marine vessel repowers, tugboat engines, locomotive upgrades, stationary equipment (generators, compressors).

title: TERP — Rebate Grants Program
eligible_entities: Entities in eligible counties including Brazoria County
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Projected opening April 2026. Up to 80% of eligible costs. Covers on-road heavy-duty diesel vehicles and select non-road equipment. Electrification eligible. Can include onsite charging infrastructure.

title: TERP — New Technology Implementation Grants (NTIG)
eligible_entities: Statewide entities implementing new emissions-reduction technologies
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Projected opening May 2026. Could fund shore power installations or innovative emissions-reduction tech at port facilities.

title: TERP — Alternative Fueling Facilities Program (AFFP)
eligible_entities: Any legal entity in the 88-county Clean Transportation Zone (includes Brazoria County)
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Most recent cycle closed January 2026; next cycle TBD. Up to $600K or 50% of eligible costs. Covers EV charging, hydrogen, CNG/LNG stations. $12M total program.

title: Texas Volkswagen Environmental Mitigation Program — All-Electric
match_requirement: No match required for government entities
eligible_entities: State and local governments, corporations in priority areas
notes: Deadline/Cycle: CURRENTLY OPEN — accepting applications through August 31, 2026. CURRENTLY OPEN. Government entities: up to 100% of incremental cost. Covers replacing diesel vehicles/equipment with all-electric + charging infrastructure. Freight switcher locomotives recently added.

title: Texas Volkswagen Environmental Mitigation Program — Locomotive/Marine Vessel
eligible_entities: Entities in priority areas of Texas
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Round 2 suspended Feb 2025; future rounds expected. Directly relevant for port harbor craft and locomotive repower. Currently suspended but future rounds anticipated.

title: Texas GLO — Coastal Management Program (CMP) Grants
match_requirement: Yes — 40% local match for NOAA-funded projects
eligible_entities: Local governments within coastal zone. Port authorities qualify.
notes: Deadline/Cycle: CURRENTLY OPEN — Cycle 32 accepting applications March 1 – June 3, 2026. CURRENTLY OPEN. Categories: coastal hazards, public access, water quality, habitat. Port Freeport is within the coastal zone.

title: Texas GLO — Coastal Erosion Planning and Response Act (CEPRA)
match_requirement: Yes — 25% for beach nourishment; 40% for other projects
eligible_entities: Any individuals or entities, public or private
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Cycle 14 active (Sept 2025 – Aug 2027). Funds erosion response, habitat restoration, shoreline stabilization. In-kind contributions may count toward match.

title: TWDB — Flood Infrastructure Fund (FIF)
match_requirement: Varies by category; some allow 100% grants
eligible_entities: Political subdivisions incl. navigation districts under TX Constitution Art. XVI, Sec. 59. Port Freeport qualifies.
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Rolling abridged applications; SFY 2027 PIFs due March 2026. $625M+ latest round. Covers stormwater infrastructure, drainage, flood control, natural system restoration. Green/nature-based projects receive additional grant %.

title: TWDB — Clean Water State Revolving Fund (CWSRF)
match_requirement: N/A — loan with potential principal forgiveness
eligible_entities: Political subdivisions including districts and authorities
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Annual; SFY 2027 PIFs due March 2026. $460M+ per year. Principal forgiveness available for disadvantaged communities or green projects — effectively converts portions to grants.

title: State and Local Cybersecurity Grant Program (SLCGP)
agency: Texas DIR / Governor's Public Safety Office
eligible_entities: Units of local government including political subdivisions. Port Freeport qualifies directly.
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Annual RFA; Year 3 closed Feb 2026; Year 4 expected ~December 2026. ~$40M over 4 years for Texas; 80%+ must pass to local governments. Must join TX-ISAO and complete cybersecurity training. Apply via eGrants. Relevant for OT/ICS/SCADA systems.

title: State Homeland Security Program (SHSP)
agency: Texas Governor's Office — Public Safety Office
eligible_entities: Local governments through regional COGs. Port Freeport applies through H-GAC.
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Annual cycle through eGrants. Port Freeport handles petrochemical operations. All projects must have nexus to terrorism prevention. Coordinate with H-GAC regional council.

title: TDEM — Hazard Mitigation Grant Program (HMGP) and BRIC
eligible_entities: Political subdivisions with FEMA-approved Local Hazard Mitigation Plan
notes: Deadline/Cycle: HMGP opens after Presidential Disaster Declarations; BRIC has annual federal cycle. Brazoria County has recent disaster declarations (2024 storms, Hurricane Beryl) that may trigger HMGP. Projects: flood mitigation, drainage, storm surge barriers, infrastructure hardening.

title: H-GAC — Clean Vehicles Program
eligible_entities: Any fleet operator with 75%+ usage in HGB nonattainment area
notes: Deadline/Cycle: ROLLING — currently accepting applications. CURRENTLY ACCEPTING. ~$30K per heavy-duty truck replacement. Covers clean diesel, alternative fuel truck replacements, marine vessel engines, CNG/LNG stations. Contact: CleanVehicles@hgac.com

title: H-GAC — Heavy Duty Diesel Replacement Program
eligible_entities: Class 6-8 on-road vehicles and non-road equipment in HGB area
notes: Deadline/Cycle: ROLLING — currently accepting applications. 50% for diesel replacement; 75% for alternative fuel/electric. Equipment must have been in use in HGB area for prior 2 years.

title: H-GAC — Transportation Alternatives Set-Aside (TASA)
eligible_entities: Cities, counties, port authorities, special districts within H-GAC 8-county region
notes: Deadline/Cycle: ~Every 2 years; SOPI forms Nov 2025–Jan 2026; questionnaire deadline Mar 2026. Port authorities explicitly listed as eligible sponsors. Projects evaluated on access/connectivity, safety, resiliency, innovation.

title: H-GAC — Subregional Planning Program
eligible_entities: Local public entities including port authorities within H-GAC region
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Periodic (~every 2 years), embedded in UPWP development. Could fund freight corridor or port access study for SH-36, Hwy 288, or intermodal connectivity.

title: H-GAC — Climate Pollution Reduction Grant (CPRG) Implementation
eligible_entities: Local governments and entities in 13-county H-GAC region
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Comprehensive plan due Dec 2025; implementation funding evolving through 2027. Port electrification and zero-emission equipment projects could emerge as priority implementation projects. Regional plan covers transportation/freight sectors.

title: H-GAC — Funding Development Program
eligible_entities: H-GAC member governments
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Annual cycle (~November). Free technical assistance for identifying funding and developing proposals. Not a direct grant — provides grant-writing support. Priorities include disaster resilience and infrastructure.

title: Skills Development Fund (SDF)
match_requirement: No cash match; employer must commit to full-time employment
eligible_entities: Public community/technical colleges or Workforce Development Boards in partnership with employer. Port Freeport partners with Brazosport College.
notes: Deadline/Cycle: ROLLING — accepts proposals year-round. Precedent: BASF Corp. partnered with Brazosport College for $373,979 SDF grant in this region. Training: maritime ops, safety, hazmat, logistics, crane operations, cybersecurity.

title: Texas Talent Connection (TTC)
eligible_entities: Partnerships of workforce boards, employers, and higher education institutions
notes: Deadline/Cycle: FY2026 deadline was March 31, 2026; annual competitive cycle. Year 1: $350K; Year 2: $250K; Year 3: $200K. Port Freeport eligible as employer partner. Could propose maritime/logistics workforce pipeline innovation project.

title: Lone Star Workforce of the Future Fund
eligible_entities: Public junior colleges and nonprofits in partnership with employer
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Rolling until funding exhausted. Up to $7,500 per trainee; max $250K per award. Created by 88th Legislature (HB 1755). At least 50% of participants must be placed in high-demand occupations.

title: SECO — LoanSTAR Revolving Loan Program
agency: State Energy Conservation Office / Texas Comptroller
eligible_entities: Texas public institutions (government buildings, public facilities)
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Open enrollment through August 31, 2026. Low-interest loans for energy retrofits: LED lighting, HVAC, building automation. Port Freeport qualifies as public entity. Not a grant, but very low interest.

title: Texas Energy Fund — Backup Power Package Program (TBPP)
eligible_entities: Critical facilities — hospitals, emergency services, water plants, shelters. Port facilities may qualify as critical infrastructure.
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Application process expected to open late 2026 / early 2027. $1.8B program. Grants up to $500/kW (max $1.25M per project at 2.5MW cap) plus 100% forgivable loans. Port eligibility uncertain — worth monitoring.

title: Transportation Reinvestment Zone (TRZ)
eligible_entities: Cities, counties, and port authorities — explicitly authorized under Texas law
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Can be created at any time following statutory process. Port Freeport designates a contiguous area as a TRZ, capturing incremental property tax revenues. Can be combined with TxDOT Pass-Through financing. No board creation required.

title: Freeport Economic Development Corporation
eligible_entities: Businesses within City of Freeport limits; infrastructure assistance negotiated case-by-case
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Ongoing. FEDC has flexibility with infrastructure funding and can negotiate case-by-case. Port Freeport could partner on joint infrastructure projects creating jobs.

title: Texas Broadband Development Office — Middle Mile Program
match_requirement: Varies; up to 100% for emergency communications
eligible_entities: Political subdivisions of Texas — Port Freeport qualifies
notes: Deadline/Cycle: Latest round closed Nov 2025; future rounds possible. $1.5B voter-approved Broadband Infrastructure Fund. Could fund critical communications infrastructure at terminal facilities. Monitor for future rounds.
